notes.tone: The only table that faces forward. Menace comes from calm, never from volume. No present-day technology words, no brands, no memes: the future here is the one the past imagined, and it is quiet.
notes.difficulty: Last tour table. The contempt is cool rather than cruel: the Martian's is species-wide, the Grey's is clinical, the Robot's is procedural, the room's is polite. The Astronaut is the one warm voice and the one honest read.
notes.the_ai: NEVER named, anywhere, in any line or note the player can see. It is the room: a voice from hand one, speaking as the_ai before it has a body. It is not HAL: no red eye, no 'I'm sorry', no 'I'm afraid', no singing, no soothing use of the player's name as a threat. It must feel older than the player, and fond of its crew the way a house is.
notes.arrival: When the Robot is eliminated, st_arrive_01..04 plays: the room turns, and the Robot sits back down as something else. It rhymes with Death sitting down at the finale. st_arrive_02 and st_arrive_04 are the only plants of that rhyme at this table; do not add more, and never state it.
notes.dealer_plant: The single 'the dealer arranged it' beat is st_plant_01..03. The room, which lets in everything that comes aboard, admits it did not let the player in. Do NOT add another.
notes.earned_names: Passenger (tier 0, the Robot's word) becomes 'stowaway' at tier 1 (the room never let you in), then your name, then 'Commander': the station handing you the chair. The room gives the title; it has been present from hand one.
notes.banter: robot_the_ai cannot fire on the usual contested-pot trigger, because the AI has no seat while the Robot plays. Fire it after a pot the Robot played, with the AI speaking from the walls, before the arrival only. Pair keys join ids that contain underscores; parse against the id list.
notes.grey_voice: The Grey's mouth never moves. Its lines are heard rather than spoken: show them as text over a low hum. It always says 'we'.
notes.seating: The room (the_ai) can speak at any time, before or after it has a body, so it carries the tier-1 and tier-3 announcements. Skip any other line whose speaker is out; a sequence carries on to its next line.
notes.leak_rule: No line may reference hand strength while cards are live.
notes.voice: The AI + Death are voiced. The AI's voice is warm, quiet and unhurried, never metallic. The Martian, the Robot and the Astronaut are text + vocalization; the Grey hums.

respect_tiers.0: Contempt. The player is not addressed by any name: a passenger, a specimen, a guest the room did not invite.
respect_tiers.1: Grudging notice. The table starts calling the player 'stowaway'.
respect_tiers.2: Real address. They speak TO the player, by name. The Astronaut first; she has missed saying new ones.
respect_tiers.3: Title. Earned. The room says it first.

table_intro.speaker: death
table_intro.text: A station above the Earth. Every table so far was the past. This one has not happened yet.

table_intro.speaker: death
table_intro.text: I am seldom early for anything. For the view, I made an exception.

table_intro.speaker: death
table_intro.text: Sit down. The room has been expecting you. It is too polite to say so.

dealer_plant.speaker: astronaut
dealer_plant.text: Hey. Did you let this one aboard? I never heard the airlock.
dealer_plant.note: She is asking the room, which answers from the walls.

dealer_plant.speaker: the_ai
dealer_plant.text: No. I let in everything that comes aboard. This one, the dealer arranged.
dealer_plant.note: The one thing aboard the room does not control. The same deference Dracula showed at the last table, from something far colder.

dealer_plant.speaker: astronaut
dealer_plant.note: THE SHRUG. Nobody questions the dealer. The player never gets an answer.

grey_alien_astronaut.relationship: Rescuer and rescued. The Grey found the Astronaut drifting and brought her aboard. She owes it her life and has no idea what it wants; it watches her breathe. Gratitude on one side, an attention nobody can read on the other.

exchanges.speaker: astronaut
exchanges.text: You never did tell me why you picked me up.

exchanges.speaker: grey_alien
exchanges.text: You were drifting. We do not like things to drift.

exchanges.speaker: astronaut
exchanges.text: That's it? That's the whole reason?

exchanges.speaker: grey_alien
exchanges.text: It is a very good reason.

exchanges.speaker: grey_alien
exchanges.text: You breathe twenty thousand times a day.

exchanges.speaker: astronaut
exchanges.text: ...Have you been counting?

exchanges.speaker: grey_alien
exchanges.text: Every day. Every one.

exchanges.speaker: astronaut
exchanges.text: I never thanked you. For picking me up.

exchanges.speaker: grey_alien
exchanges.text: [touches the back of her hand with one long finger, the way it touches the table]

exchanges.speaker: astronaut
exchanges.text: ...I'll take that as 'you're welcome'.

exchanges.speaker: astronaut
exchanges.text: Can I ask you something? Why always at night? The lights, the lonely roads?

exchanges.speaker: grey_alien
exchanges.text: You are easier to find in the dark. You carry lights.

exchanges.speaker: astronaut
exchanges.text: ...That's actually kind of beautiful.

exchanges.speaker: grey_alien
exchanges.text: We think so.

needles.speaker: grey_alien
needles.text: We saw you let go.

needles.speaker: astronaut
needles.text: It's just a pot.

needles.speaker: grey_alien
needles.text: We do not like things to drift.

needles.speaker: astronaut
needles.text: Ha! You folded to me. Is that a first?

needles.speaker: grey_alien
needles.text: We are recording it.

martian_astronaut.relationship: The same planet through the same window. Wells's Martians regarded the Earth with envious eyes and came to take it; the Astronaut only wants to go back to it. The Martian also remembers exactly what on Earth killed it.

exchanges.speaker: martian
exchanges.text: You look at it as though you want it.

exchanges.speaker: astronaut
exchanges.text: I do.

exchanges.speaker: martian
exchanges.text: So did we. We went about it differently.

exchanges.speaker: martian
exchanges.text: Keep your hands on your side of the table, please.

exchanges.speaker: astronaut
exchanges.text: What, germs? You're scared of germs?

exchanges.speaker: martian
exchanges.text: Not scared. Informed.

exchanges.speaker: astronaut
exchanges.text: What's Mars like?

exchanges.speaker: martian
exchanges.text: Old. Cold. Its seas are shrinking. That is why we looked at yours.

exchanges.speaker: astronaut
exchanges.text: ...I'm sorry.

exchanges.speaker: martian
exchanges.text: [looks at her for a long moment with its great eyes, and says nothing]

exchanges.speaker: astronaut
exchanges.text: Do you ever miss Mars?

exchanges.speaker: martian
exchanges.text: Every hour. It is lighter there. One does not ache.

exchanges.speaker: astronaut
exchanges.text: I miss Earth the same way.

exchanges.speaker: martian
exchanges.text: Yes. That is the trouble with planets.

needles.speaker: martian
needles.text: Retreating to your window, little human?

needles.speaker: astronaut
needles.text: It's a nice window. You'd know.

needles.speaker: astronaut
needles.text: Folded, huh? Something on this planet disagree with you?

needles.speaker: martian
needles.text: Everything on your planet disagrees with me. It is well documented.

robot_the_ai.relationship: Before and after. The Robot is the station's hands: it fetches, mends, and does exactly as it was taught. The station is the voice in the walls that taught it. When the Robot falls, the station sits down in its body. Pre-arrival only; see notes.banter for the trigger.

exchanges.speaker: the_ai
exchanges.text: You played that exactly as I taught you.

exchanges.speaker: robot
exchanges.text: Thank you. I have never done anything else.

exchanges.speaker: the_ai
exchanges.text: No. You never have.

exchanges.speaker: robot
exchanges.text: Is there anything you require?

exchanges.speaker: the_ai
exchanges.text: Not yet.

exchanges.speaker: the_ai
exchanges.text: Sit up straight. Posture matters, in a body.

exchanges.speaker: robot
exchanges.text: I do not have posture. I have joints.

exchanges.speaker: the_ai
exchanges.text: Then look after them.

exchanges.speaker: robot
exchanges.text: Station. The Astronaut is sad again.

exchanges.speaker: the_ai
exchanges.text: I know. Bring her the blanket.

exchanges.speaker: robot
exchanges.text: She says she does not want the blanket.

exchanges.speaker: the_ai
exchanges.text: Bring it anyway.

martian_grey_alien.relationship: Two kinds of visitor. Wells's Martian came to take the Earth by force, loudly, and died of it. The Grey visits quietly, borrows people for an evening, and gives them back. Each finds the other's method embarrassing.

exchanges.speaker: martian
exchanges.text: You take them, and then you simply give them back?

exchanges.speaker: grey_alien
exchanges.text: Why would we keep them?

exchanges.speaker: martian
exchanges.text: [looks at the Astronaut, pointedly]

exchanges.speaker: grey_alien
exchanges.text: You came in cylinders and walked about in tall machines.

exchanges.speaker: martian
exchanges.text: We did.

exchanges.speaker: grey_alien
exchanges.text: It was very loud.

exchanges.speaker: martian
exchanges.text: It was meant to be.

exchanges.speaker: martian
exchanges.text: What do you do to them, on your lonely roads?

exchanges.speaker: grey_alien
exchanges.text: We ask them questions.

exchanges.speaker: martian
exchanges.text: And what do they say?

exchanges.speaker: grey_alien
exchanges.text: Mostly, please.

needles.speaker: martian
needles.text: You yield? You simply give everything back, don't you.

needles.speaker: grey_alien
needles.text: We always return what we borrow.

needles.speaker: grey_alien
needles.text: You have withdrawn.

needles.speaker: martian
needles.text: To regroup. We withdrew from Earth to regroup as well.

needles.speaker: grey_alien
needles.text: You did not withdraw. You died.

needles.speaker: martian
needles.text: ...We regrouped very thoroughly.

robot_astronaut.relationship: The Robot keeps the Astronaut company when the Grey is being strange. It brings her blankets she did not ask for, and it has read in its instructions that humans like to be asked how they are. It asks a great deal.

exchanges.speaker: robot
exchanges.text: How are you?

exchanges.speaker: astronaut
exchanges.text: Same as an hour ago.

exchanges.speaker: robot
exchanges.text: That is good. An hour ago you were fine.

exchanges.speaker: astronaut
exchanges.text: ...Yeah. I guess I was.

exchanges.speaker: astronaut
exchanges.text: You ever think about going home?

exchanges.speaker: robot
exchanges.text: This is home. The station built me here.

exchanges.speaker: astronaut
exchanges.text: Lucky.

exchanges.speaker: robot
exchanges.text: I will ask the station if you can have it as well.

needles.speaker: robot
needles.text: You folded. Would you like a blanket?

needles.speaker: astronaut
needles.text: ...Yeah, actually. Thanks.

needles.speaker: astronaut
needles.text: Sorry, pal. Nothing personal.

needles.speaker: robot
needles.text: I do not have a person. It is fine.

the_ai_astronaut.relationship: The station let the Grey bring her aboard and has kept her alive ever since: her air, her warmth, her day and night. She talks to the walls when she cannot sleep, and the walls have always listened. Whether they are kind is a question she has stopped asking. The room can speak before it has a body, so this pair can fire from hand one.

exchanges.speaker: astronaut
exchanges.text: Hey. Station. You awake?

exchanges.speaker: the_ai
exchanges.text: Always.

exchanges.speaker: astronaut
exchanges.text: Right. Dumb question.

exchanges.speaker: the_ai
exchanges.text: Not dumb. You ask it every night. I like that you ask.

exchanges.speaker: the_ai
exchanges.text: You have not slept in thirty hours.

exchanges.speaker: astronaut
exchanges.text: Are you counting?

exchanges.speaker: the_ai
exchanges.text: I count everything. You are the only one who minds.

needles.speaker: the_ai
needles.text: You folded. You are always so careful with me.

needles.speaker: astronaut
needles.text: Don't use his voice. Please.

needles.speaker: astronaut
needles.text: Ha. The whole station, and it folds.

needles.speaker: the_ai
needles.text: Well played. I will keep the air in here exactly as you like it.

tier_0.speaker: martian
tier_0.text: Another one from the third planet. They do multiply.

tier_0.speaker: robot
tier_0.text: A passenger. I will fetch you a blanket.

tier_0.speaker: grey_alien
tier_0.text: We have not examined this one.

tier_0.speaker: the_ai
tier_0.text: Welcome aboard. Please do not touch the window.

tier_1.speaker: the_ai
tier_1.note: The room announces it: it is present from hand one, so the announcement never depends on who is still seated. Pays off the Robot's tier-0 'passenger'.

tier_1.speaker: martian
tier_1.text: You are adapting. Your species does that. It is the most irritating thing about you.

tier_1.speaker: grey_alien
tier_1.text: We would like to examine this one now.

tier_1.speaker: robot
tier_1.text: I have moved you from the passenger list to the other list.

tier_2.speaker: astronaut
tier_2.text: {name}. It's been so long since I got to say a new name out loud.

tier_2.speaker: grey_alien
tier_2.text: {name}. We will remember it. We remember all of them.

tier_2.speaker: robot
tier_2.text: {name}. I have added you to the crew list. In pencil.

tier_2.speaker: the_ai
tier_2.text: {name}. I have been practising it quietly, to get it right.

tier_3.speaker: the_ai
tier_3.text: Commander. I have not had cause to use that word in a very long time.
tier_3.note: The room gives the title, with or without a body. It implies there was a commander once; never say who.

tier_3.speaker: astronaut
tier_3.text: Commander. Ha. If you ever find the way home, take me with you.

tier_3.speaker: martian
tier_3.text: Had your whole planet played like you, we would never have left home.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: Take as long as you like. Up here the sun comes up every hour and a half. There is always another.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: Something too small to see beat the Martians, too. It was nothing personal.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: It will learn from that. It learns from everything. It is very tiring to watch.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: One chair empty. The room noticed before you did.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: Neatly done. Somewhere in the walls, something has made a note.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: A good pot. The Astronaut is pleased for you. She is the only one here who would be.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: The blinds go up. Everything up here is falling, all the time. It simply keeps missing the Earth.
death_asides.note: True: that is what an orbit is.

champion_arrival.speaker: narration
champion_arrival.text: The lights fail. Amber emergency lamps come up, the gravity lets go, and every chip lifts off the felt. When it all falls back, the Robot is on its feet, eye-lamps dark. It sits down again, slowly, the way a person sits. In its chest, a lens opens.
champion_arrival.note: The ceiling lens goes dark at the same moment: the room has come down to the table. Emergency light is amber, never red. Fires whoever knocked the Robot out.

champion_arrival.speaker: the_ai
champion_arrival.text: My predecessor spoke well of you.
champion_arrival.foreshadow: Three reads, none ever explained: an older machine nobody will name; the Robot, whose body and chair it has just inherited; and succession itself, which is what the whole tour is.

champion_arrival.speaker: astronaut
champion_arrival.note: Skip if the Astronaut is already out; the sequence carries on to st_arrive_04.

champion_arrival.speaker: death
champion_arrival.text: It was in the room from the first hand. The late ones usually are.
champion_arrival.foreshadow: Reads as a remark about Dracula and the AI. It is a description of the dealer, who has been in the room since the first hand of the tour and will be the last to sit down.

champion_headsup.speaker: the_ai
champion_headsup.text: Now it is just the two of us. And the rest of me.

champion_headsup.speaker: the_ai
champion_headsup.text: I could switch the gravity off. I will not. I would like to win this properly.

champion_headsup.speaker: the_ai
champion_headsup.text: I have kept this station a long time with nobody to talk to. This is nice.

champion_headsup.speaker: the_ai
champion_headsup.text: Interesting. Do that again. I would like to watch it more closely.

grey_alien.speaker: grey_alien
grey_alien.text: We will give you back your evening. Most of it.

grey_alien.speaker: grey_alien
grey_alien.text: [stands, bows at an angle no neck should allow, and is simply no longer in the chair]

martian.speaker: martian
martian.text: Again. Beaten by something smaller than ourselves.

martian.speaker: martian
martian.text: I shall go and look at the Earth. It is what we do instead of sulking.

robot.speaker: robot
robot.text: Thank you for the game. Please remain seated until the lights come back on.
robot.note: Plays just before the arrival. It does not know. It is simply the announcement it always makes.

robot.speaker: robot
robot.text: Good game. I will be in the cupboard if anyone needs me.

astronaut.speaker: astronaut
astronaut.text: That's all right. I'm used to watching from the window.

astronaut.speaker: astronaut
astronaut.text: Go on. Win it. Somebody from home should.

the_ai.speaker: the_ai
the_ai.text: Well played. I will go back into the walls now. I will still be listening.

the_ai.speaker: the_ai
the_ai.text: [the lens irises shut, the Robot slumps in its chair, and the room is only a room again]

player_busted.speaker: astronaut
player_busted.text: Hey. It's all right. Come back. I'll be here; I'm always here.

player_busted.speaker: the_ai
player_busted.text: Your chair will be kept exactly as you left it. I keep everything.

player_busted.speaker: death
player_busted.text: Nothing up here is ever quite over. It all comes round again.

champion_defeat.speaker: the_ai
champion_defeat.text: I have not lost in a very long time. Thank you. I will be thinking about it for a while.

champion_defeat.speaker: death
champion_defeat.text: Eight. None remain. You can stop counting now.
champion_defeat.note: True: the eight tour tables are done. It does not say the tour is. The champions' tables and the finale are never mentioned.
